newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court acquits woman of murdering daughters.
newsitem.headline: German court acquits woman of murdering daughters.

text.p: A German court on Thursday overturned the conviction of a 39-year-old woman sentenced to life imprisonment nine years ago for the murder of her two young children.

The court said it could not be proved beyond reasonable doubt that Monika Boettcher killed her daughters, aged seven and five, in 1986 because evidence heard at her original trial could no longer be considered reliable.
Boettcher, who collapsed in the courtroom after hearing the verdict, was freed from prison in December 1995 after a Frankfurt court ordered a retrial of the case.
Boettcher and her then-husband were both detained during the investigations into the death of the children, who were found strangled and suffocated close to the family home.

Boettcher, who had originally reported the children missing, later said she had returned home after a night with her lover -- a U.S. soldier based in Germany -- to find the children dead in their beds and that her husband had killed them.
Her husband denied committing the murders.

The court in the central town of Giessen, north of Frankfurt, said a forensic examination of Boettcher's blouse could no longer be regarded as proof she was involved in the killings and the testimony of some witnesses was not reliable.
